guidance.heading: FULL-YEAR 2026 OUTLOOK
section: The Company's outlook reflects the impact of foreign currency and includes the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds received in the third quarter. The Company's previous outlook did not include any benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. Additionally, fiscal 2026 is a 52-week year and fiscal 2025 was a 53-week year, which will affect annual comparisons.

desk.headline: Revenue up 7.5% to $505m, adjusted EPS $0.79 beat (incl. ~$0.31 tariff refund); 2026 outlook raised

other.label: Gross margin
other.change: +710 bps y/y (about 640 bps from tariff refunds)

results: Revenue rose 7.5% to $505m, the eighth quarter of growth in a row; Active Group grew 9.9% while Work Group was up just 0.9%.
Saucony led with 19% growth and Merrell grew 6.5%; Wolverine (-4%) and Sweaty Betty (-7%) shrank. International sales rose 12%.
The company received $35.3m of refunds on IEEPA tariffs it had paid, which lifted gross and operating margins by about 6.4 points and EPS by about $0.31.
Adjusted EPS more than doubled to $0.79 (GAAP $0.78), well above the $0.46 estimate even before the refund benefit.
Net debt fell 26% to $399m and inventory was 5% lower than a year ago.

guidance.summary: Wolverine raised its 2026 outlook for revenue, margins and EPS. The new numbers include about $0.32 of EPS benefit from tariff refunds, which the earlier outlook left out.

points: The CEO credited the two largest brands, Merrell and Saucony, and tight execution for the quarter.
He described the turnaround as now also a growth story, with eight straight quarters of growth.
A stronger balance sheet is said to give more room to invest behind the brands.
Management still calls the environment dynamic, but raised the outlook on year-to-date results and Q4 expectations.
call.source: No call coverage found; points from CEO comments in the results release

watch: Q4 delivery against the raised outlook, and how margins look once the one-off tariff refunds fall away.
Whether Saucony keeps growing near 20% and whether Wolverine and Sweaty Betty return to growth.
Further debt reduction and direct-to-consumer sales, which grew only 2%.
